lenses.name: Emission channel and one-shot latch reachability

findings.claim: alias pays the full 4.1s ceiling whenever the running daemon is alive but cannot publish: an origin/main daemon after a CLI upgrade, or a daemon started with PORTLESS_SYNC_HOSTS=0. hasLiveHostsSyncPublisher proves liveness, not capability.
findings.evidence: Built origin/main, started its daemon, ran the PR CLI: alias 4.18s. PR daemon started with sync disabled: 4.17s. Controls: no daemon 0.04s, capable daemon 0.15s.

findings.claim: The inverse direction of the same root cause, not reported externally: a CLI invoked with PORTLESS_SYNC_HOSTS=0 against an enabled daemon suppresses a real sync failure entirely. reportHostsSyncAfterRouteChange reads the CLI's own env to decide what the daemon will do.
findings.evidence: Enabled daemon, then PORTLESS_SYNC_HOSTS=0 portless alias split 18186: returned 0.06s, no warning. One second later proxy.hosts-sync-status held ok:false with the full warning, and proxy.log had the same failure.

findings.claim: portless clean leaves proxy.hosts-sync-status behind, registered hostnames included; PID-suffixed temp files are not expressible by the static allowlist at all.
findings.evidence: Created the status file, ran the built portless clean: it printed 'Removed portless state files' and 'Clean finished' while find still returned proxy.hosts-sync-status. Both artifacts and surfaces gates flagged it.

findings.claim: All five surfaces promise the sync failure 'warns once', but the latch is daemon-scoped while delivery is per-CLI-process, so a user registering two apps is warned twice. Not reported externally and not caught in six rounds.
findings.evidence: Two successive built-CLI calls, alias second and alias third, both printed the warning (0.15s, 0.14s) while the daemon log held one. Wording confirmed at README.md:483, SKILL.md:414, apps/docs page.mdx:114, commands/page.mdx:274, cli.ts:2016.
